messages:
maria (eng-security): Heads up — noticing a cluster of high-rate reads against sensitive tables from the read-proxy. Looks like the requests are authenticated as analytics-svc but hitting billing.chargeback rows. Put a quick watch on it.

sam (dba): can you paste an example query / raw log line?

maria (eng-security): log snippet: 
```
2026-03-20T15:04:12Z GET /db/proxy/query 200 user=analytics-svc route=/v1/query query=\"SELECT id,acct_id,amount FROM billing.chargeback WHERE created_at > '2026-03-01' LIMIT 10000\"
headers: x-auth-method=token x-auth-source=read-proxy x-request-id=req_0a1b2c
```
The rate is ~120 qps sustained for ~7m. This path shouldn't allow analytics-svc to read billing.chargeback.

jyoti (sre): audit-bot just posted a matching alert: `db-read-anomaly` w/ score 0.92. I've flagged the proxy route and started capturing full reqs.

audit-bot: Found 17 matching audit events in last 10m. Service account=analytics-svc, principal_kind=service_account, auth_method=token, action=SELECT, resources=[billing.chargeback]. Log IDs: [A-9843, A-9844, A-9851].

kevin (platform): quick checks: KMS usage for export keys looks normal but I see several decrypt calls from the analytics service principal at 15:02-15:07 that line up. Not yet indicating an external key compromise.

sam (dba): does analytics-svc normally have any RBAC to billing.*? policy lookup: `role: analytics_read` -> resource list does NOT include billing.chargeback. Who recently changed roles?\
maria (eng-security): cross-ref with IAM audit: there is a policy update PR merged 3h ago: infra/iam#1423 by taylor — it removed `legacy-analytics-role` and mapped service accounts to `analytics_read_v2`. Might be a policy regression.\
taylor (infra): that PR was intended to consolidate roles. I added a mapping table, but I did not intentionally grant billing access. I'll re-open the PR and diff the final policy.\
jyoti (sre): containment plan: (1) revoke analytics-svc token, (2) temporarily block read-proxy route for analytics-svc in the authz layer, (3) snapshot current logs and S3 actions. I'll take (1) and (2) now.

maria (eng-security): do it. Also, rotate any short-lived keys associated with analytics-svc post-revocation and add to incident runbook.

kevin (platform): started rotation: triggering `kms:Revoke` for service-account key alias/analytics-svc. Also checking object ACLs for recent PUTs.

sam (dba): I queried S3 audit logs: found one PUT at 2026-03-20T15:06:20 to bucket redwood-exports-prod/analytics/2026-03-20/report-8d2c.csv (size 12MB) from IP 54.210.99.10. The PUT was performed using internal exporter lambda role `exports-job`.

maria (eng-security): that suggests the SELECTs might have been part of an internal export job that unintentionally gained additional table scope. But we still need to confirm intent and who triggered export.

jyoti (sre): I've disabled the proxy route mapping for analytics-svc. authz now returns 403 for requests that would hit billing.* from that SA. Token revocation completed (`kubectl delete secret analytics-svc-token -n infra`).

kevin (platform): KMS revoke completed, but note: rotating the alias will not invalidate objects already encrypted with the old key — we need to confirm whether exported object was encrypted-at-rest via KMS or client-side. S3 metadata: x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms, x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id=arn:aws:kms:...:key/abc123. That key had decrypt calls by analytics-svc earlier.

sam (dba): creating a read-only copy of the export for investigation. Also queried DB audit: the SELECTs originated from a job-id header: job=exports-job-20260320-1. Owner looks like `exports-service` (not analytics-svc). There's a mismatch between auth principal and job header.

maria (eng-security): action: open INC-2345 (created). Root-owner: maria. Tasks: 1) confirm whether PR infra/iam#1423 unintentionally expanded scope (owner taylor) 2) confirm who triggered exports-job and why auth principal was analytics-svc (owner sam) 3) rotate KMS keys and service tokens (owners kevin/jyoti) 4) preserve evidence and follow chain of custody (owner maria).

taylor (infra): digging into the merged policy diff now. Preliminary: a mapping change accidentally preserved an old wildcard in `resource_pattern: billing.*` for tenants flagged `legacy=true`. That looks like my regression. Going to revert and push a constrained rule.

audit-bot: Recorded incident INC-2345. Evidence bundle created: logs A-9843..A-9860, S3 object redwood-exports-prod/analytics/2026-03-20/report-8d2c.csv, IAM policy diff at infra/iam#1423@merge.

kevin (platform): I'll mark the exported object as quarantined and change its ACL to private, copy to investigation bucket `redwood-sec-investigation/INC-2345/`. Starting copy now.

maria (eng-security): good. Sam — can you confirm whether exports-job has any downstream external destinations (ftp/s3 external accounts)?

sam (dba): exports-job config: destinations: s3:redwood-exports-prod (internal), slack-notify (internal). No external FTP. Recent runs show only this bucket.

jyoti (sre): monitoring in place. If we see any more decrypt calls by analytics-svc or requests from IP 54.210.99.10, alert and escalate to P1 channel.

maria (eng-security): interim judgement: likely internal misconfiguration caused by infra/iam PR; not an external credential compromise. Still treat as incident until policy revert, token rotations, and 24h monitoring complete.

kevin (platform): policy revert PR submitted: infra/iam#1427 (revert partial mapping). I'm also adding a test in CI that asserts analytics_read_v2 does not include billing.*.

taylor (infra): will follow up with postmortem: root cause, timeline, and proposed guardrails (policy CI tests, approval steps for role changes). Also tagging ops-safety for future runbook updates.

maria (eng-security): timeline summary for the PM: 15:02 detection -> 15:07 containment (token revoked + route blocked) -> 15:15 export object quarantined -> 15:30 policy revert PR open. Next steps: 24h monitoring, rotate any related KMS/SA creds, postmortem doc and preventive controls.

sam (dba): I've attached the export SQL and job metadata to INC-2345.

jyoti (sre): leaving monitoring on. Will close this thread here and move live updates to the incident ticket.

maria (eng-security): thanks team — marking action items in the ticket. Will send a short blameless summary to leadership after the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
